question: Can a deterministic sweeper report doc-lifecycle problems (timestamps, age/status, index drift, broken links) cheaply and accurately?
notes: All 5 pre-existing docs without front-matter (capabilities, decisions, doc-lifecycle, landscape, workflow) reported as missing-created/missing-updated errors; none edited.
Index drift: decisions.md, plans/2026-10-02-spike-phase.md, specs/2026-10-02-agent-swarm-design.md not linked from ../AGENTS.md or ../README.md (direct links only, not transitive).
Plan/spec use status values 'executing' and 'draft-for-review' that the convention (current|stale?|archived) does not list; reported as warnings.
Every doc is 0 days old on 2026-10-02, so no age-based findings on the real corpus; thresholds only exercised by testdata.
Proposed thresholds: design decision 90d, device fact 180d, benchmark 30d, default 90d, archive at 2x; see RESULTS.md
howToRun: dotnet run sweep.cs -- <docsDir> [--today 2026-10-02] [--json]   |   dotnet run sweep.cs -- --selftest
